ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To cut off is to sever a flow, entanglement, division, or opening for continuation.
EvidenceBody: An unnamed monk asks Guitong Huitong about the line that cuts off all streams. Yuanwu Keqin sings of cutting off all streams; Baiyu Jingsi and Dahui Zonggao speak of cutting through entanglements; Shoushan Xingnian says one word cuts off a thousand river mouths; Konggu Daocheng answers that sticks and shouts do not accommodate human feeling.

Senses.Note: 8 exact witnesses from 8 independent works delimit this sense.
